purpose: Defines what may execute as part of realpass. Gameplay and presentation behavior must be authored and owned by realpass; source mods are reference material only. realpass is vanilla-first: preserve CDPR identities/surfaces where useful and substitute project-original mechanics beneath them.

releaseExperience.note: Internal module gates may exist during development and acceptance, but a release build enables the complete accepted realpass experience as one product. Mod Settings exposes exactly one binary presentation preference for the RealPass-owned E3-inspired first-person HUD/nameplate skin; it does not change simulation authority.

vanillaFirst.rule: Keep vanilla item/system names, identities, animations, screens/assets and interaction language where they can host the realism model. Replace mechanics underneath instead of importing source-mod renames or duplicating the vanilla surface.

runtimeOwnership.frameworkRule: A framework may expose APIs, script loading, data loading, UI primitives or input plumbing. It may not supply the body, combat, injury, armor, presentation or progression behavior that defines realpass.
runtimeOwnership.referenceRule: Third-party gameplay/presentation mods may be studied and retained as provenance/reference records, but their scripts, archives, tweak payloads and assets may not be required by or packaged into the standalone RealPass runtime. The E3 visual target must therefore be recreated in RealPass-owned code/assets rather than executed from the source mod.

genericInfrastructure.modSettingsBoundary: Mod Settings provides exactly one RealPass public control: the binary E3-inspired first-person HUD/nameplate presentation preference. Guarded listener registration/persistence is allowed. Mod Settings is not a body, injury, combat, armor, progression or balance authority.

developmentRules: Internal modules may be independently gated to isolate faults and calibrate systems.
Development gates are not player preferences and must not become a release configuration menu.
A development candidate advertised as owned-runtime must fail closed if Dark Future or Project E3 executing content is present in its deployment manifest.
A development candidate advertised as owned-runtime must preserve vanilla item/system identity and reject inherited source-mod item renames.
The current owned candidate may stage only the generic infrastructure explicitly listed as required; adding another framework requires an owned-source need and synchronized contract change.
Reference recipes may remain in the repository for historical provenance but may not feed the standalone owned-runtime builder.
No source-mod save state may be required to initialize a clean realpass save/runtime.
releaseRules: The accepted body, injury, combat, armor, cyberware-physiology and presentation authorities ship together.
The release has one authored balance rather than exposing subsystem disable switches.
The sole public preference may disable the RealPass-owned E3-inspired HUD/nameplate visual skin only; it cannot change simulation or restore source-mod runtime ownership.
Traditional actor health bars are intentionally not part of the final authored RealPass presentation once replacement feedback is accepted.
External gameplay/presentation mods are optional user choices outside realpass and are not prerequisites, bundled payloads or hidden runtime hosts.
Generic framework dependencies may be bundled only when explicitly required as infrastructure and properly licensed/noticed; they never become gameplay/presentation policy owners.
Vanilla item/system identities are preserved unless a future explicit product goal authorizes a replacement identity.
Every runtime file in the realpass-owned payload must have explicit provenance.
